title: shared_mutable_placeholder flags every module-level singleton accessor (`_CLIENT = Client()`, a ThreadPoolExecutor, an Engine, a cache dict) and has no marker, allow list or baseline
failure_scenario: A consumer with a lazy-singleton accessor (`def get_executor(): return _EXEC`, `def session(): return _SESSION`) is blocked on correct code. The only escape the API offers is passing a narrower file list, which turns the gate off for the whole file, including its real defects (a `_EMPTY = []` default handed to callers in the same file).
proposed_fix: Add `allow: Mapping[str,str]` (relpath::function -> reason) and a `# shared-ok: <reason>` marker on the return line or the assignment, and a baseline_path like the other ratchets. Narrow the placeholder test: a capitalised call counts only for a short list of container-like classes (Rows-style) or when the module also mutates the name (`.append`, `[k] =`, `.update`) in a function that is not the returner; a never-mutated singleton is not a placeholder.

title: fail_open_handlers `silent_default_return` flags ordinary control-flow exceptions (StopIteration, KeyError, queue.Empty, ProcessLookupError, ZeroDivisionError, AttributeError, TimeoutError, CancelledError, UnicodeDecodeError, JSONDecodeError, CalledProcessError) in any function
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/probe_foh.py (find_fail_open_handlers on one-handler functions): stopiter, keyerror, queue_empty, proclookup, timeout, zerodiv, attr, unicode, jsondec, notimpl, oserror_isdir, calledproc, valueerror_multi, cancel, keyerror_pop, lookup_error_check, getkey_gate_false all -> ['silent_default_return']. Example: `def lookup(d,k):\n try: return d[k]\n except KeyError: return None` (same meaning as `d.get(k)`) is reported. src/py_ci_shared/fail_open_handlers.py:325-336 (`_silent_default_return`) exempts only message-carrying returns, ImportError, FileNotFoundError, cache/stamp/token/digest/signature/key/encode/freeze names, sqlite OperationalError reads. The module docstring says 'Fail-open exception handlers in gate code', but this rule applies to every function.
failure_scenario: A repo adopting the gate gets one finding per `except KeyError: return None` / `except queue.Empty: return None` / `os.kill` probe. The only escapes are the per-handler `# best-effort:` comment (which asserts the fallback 'cannot change a result', not true for a lookup miss that the caller branches on) or the baseline; autopsia already carries 39 such keys (audits/2026-11-04/37 per-key table).
proposed_fix: Add a 'reasoned control-flow exception' set: a handler whose caught names are all in {StopIteration, StopAsyncIteration, KeyError, IndexError, queue.Empty, ProcessLookupError, ZeroDivisionError, asyncio.CancelledError, asyncio.TimeoutError} and whose try body is one expression/statement (a lookup, a next(), a wait_for, a kill) is not a silent default. Keep OSError, Exception and bare except flagged.

title: CHANGELOG 'Gate false positives 2026-11-06' says a single-value parse guard (`int(x)` / `except ValueError: return default`) is no longer flagged; the code and its tests still flag it
evidence:
CHANGELOG.md 'Gate false positives 2026-11-06', bullet 'silent_default_return no longer flags two more reasoned fallbacks: a handler whose try body only parses one value (int, float, ...) and that catches only ValueError/TypeError'. Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p6.py: `def max_workers():

failure_scenario: A consumer reads the CHANGELOG, expects `_float_env` / `_age_years` baseline entries to go stale and shrink, and instead keeps seeing them (or removes them by hand and goes red). The 13-key shrink the CHANGELOG reports for autopsia (8 sqlite + 5 parse) is overstated by the parse half.
proposed_fix: Decide the rule and make the three places agree. If a bad env value that keeps its default IS a fail-open (the 37 per-key decision), edit the CHANGELOG bullet to say so and drop the 5 value-parse keys from the '13' count. If it is not, delete the two tests and add the parse-guard exemption the CHANGELOG describes. Add a meta test that every 'no longer flags' CHANGELOG bullet in a 'Gate false positives' section names a test (changelog_promise_parity already exists for README claims; extend it).

title: `# literal-set-ok:` exempts only the `literal-set` rule; the `threshold` and `named-constant` rules of drifted_duplicate_literals have no marker, so numeric-zero floors and per-kernel constants can only be baselined
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p5.py: three modules each `return std < 1e-12  # literal-set-ok: float floor` (marker on the line and the line above) -> 1 [threshold] finding; two modules `# literal-set-ok: own crossover\nSWEEP_ROWS = 7777` -> 1 [named-constant] finding. src/py_ci_shared/drifted_duplicate_literals.py:383-385 (`_separate_measurement`) and :407-411 apply the marker only to `a` (tuple/ladder/text sites), `constants += b` and `compares += c` are unfiltered. CHANGELOG 37-F37 text and docstring name the mechanism generically. Consumer evidence: mlframe tests/test_meta/_drifted_threshold_literals_baseline.json carries 9 entries, 7 of them 'Numerical-zero guard on a dispersion/denominator ... floating-point safety floor' (1e-9, 1e-12 and 1e-300 compared against std/var/norm/denom names across 20+ modules).
failure_scenario: Every kernel module that guards a division with its own `std < 1e-12` joins one threshold group; a consumer that follows the 37-F37 advice and writes the marker still fails, and has no per-site escape: it must freeze the group in a baseline, which then silently covers a real drift of that value.
proposed_fix: Apply `_separate_measurement` to `b` and `c` as well (same marker, or a second marker `# threshold-ok: <reason>`), and add 1e-6..1e-300 epsilon floors compared against a variance/std/norm/denominator name to the default ignore of the threshold rule (a float safety floor is not a tuned limit).

title: no_source_text_tests reports any upper-case SQL keyword in a membership assert whatever the right operand is (HTTP Allow header, event list, dict keys, set of operations)
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p8.py: `assert 'DELETE' in resp.headers['Allow']`, `assert 'UPDATE' in events`, `assert 'SELECT' in actions`, `assert 'FROM' in msg.keys()`, `assert 'ORDER BY' in row`, `assert 'INSERT' in {r.op for r in result}` -> 1 [source-text-test] finding each. src/py_ci_shared/no_source_text_tests.py:36-40 and SQL_PROBE at :40; the rule never looks at what the right side is. 37-F14 fixed prose containing 'FROM' only when the literal is a sentence.
failure_scenario: A REST test that checks the allowed methods, a state-machine test over enum names `INSERT`/`UPDATE`, or an email-header test is flagged as a source-text probe. The only exits are a baseline or the whole-file exclusion.
proposed_fix: Judge only when the right operand is a str-typed expression: a name containing sql/query/stmt/statement/text/body/rendered, a call returning str (`str(...)`, `.format`, `compile(...)`), or an f-string. Skip a right operand that is `.headers[...]`, `.keys()`, a set/list/dict display or comprehension, or a name ending in s (collection).

title: env_flag_parsing reports numeric and path-like variables read by truthiness or compared with '0'/'1' whenever the variable name is not on its short word list
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p8.py with prefix MYP_: `n = os.environ.get('MYP_JOBS')\n if n: return int(n)` -> [MYP_JOBS (truthiness in a condition)]; `if os.environ.get('MYP_CACHE'): ...` -> flagged; `if os.environ.get('MYP_DEVICE')` -> flagged; `os.environ.get('MYP_RETRIES') == '0'` -> flagged (compared with '0'); `os.environ.get('MYP_VERBOSITY') == '1'` -> flagged. Not flagged: MYP_MODE=='fast', MYP_API_TOKEN, MYP_LOG_LEVEL or 'info'. 37-F8/F32 narrowed by NAME only (path, number, URL, host, credential words).
failure_scenario: A repo with `MYPROJ_JOBS`, `MYPROJ_CACHE`, `MYPROJ_RETRIES`, `MYPROJ_VERBOSITY` is told to route them through a boolean env parser, which would turn `MYPROJ_RETRIES=3` into `True`. Following the gate's advice breaks the code.
proposed_fix: Use the data flow in the same function: a read whose value (or the local it is bound to) reaches `int()`, `float()`, `Path()`, `os.path.*`, `.split`, `.isdigit` or an arithmetic operator is not a boolean flag. Compare with '0'/'1' counts only when no numeric use of the same value exists.

title: fail_open_handlers still flags fail-closed verification and deny helpers (`return False` in `is_allowed`, `check_ready`, MAC and signature checks); only names containing 'signature' or 'token' escape by accident
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/probe_foh.py and C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p6.py: `def is_allowed(x): try: return policy(x) except Exception: return False` -> silent_default_return; `def check_ready(c): try: c.ping(); return True except ConnectionError: return False` -> silent_default_return; `def cuda_ok(): try: import cupy; return cupy.cuda.is_available() except Exception: return False` -> flagged; `def verify_signature(b): try: check(b) except Exception: return False` -> NOT flagged only because src/py_ci_shared/fail_open_handlers.py:252 `_CACHE_MISS_NAME_RE` matches 'signature'. audits/2026-11-04/37 per-key table lists 9 autopsia keys 'kept flagged: fail-closed' (`_is_trusted`, `load_verified`, `trailer_mac`, `signed_pickle`, `cupy_device_usable`, ...).
failure_scenario: The exemption by function name is inconsistent: `trailer_mac` and `_is_trusted` stay flagged, `verify_signature` does not. A returned False/None from a verifier is the safe direction (denial), so the finding names a defect that is not there, and the name regex also hides a real fail-open in a function called `get_token` that returns a default credential.
proposed_fix: Replace the name regex for fail-closed: a handler that returns a falsy literal (False, None, 0, '') in a function whose result is used as a boolean predicate (name starts with is_/has_/can_/verify/check/valid or ends with _ok/_trusted) and whose caller treats False as deny is exempt; remove 'token' and 'digest' from `_CACHE_MISS_NAME_RE` or require the try body to be a cache read.

title: pickle_state_completeness `unpicklable-without-getstate` flags every class that assigns a Thread, lock or connection outside __init__, including classes that are never pickled; no marker
evidence:
Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p9.py and C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p10.py: `class Worker:
 def start(self):
  self._thread = threading.Thread(target=print)
  self._thread.start()` -> 'Worker.start sets self._thread = threading.Thread(...) and Worker defines no __getstate__/__reduce__'. src/py_ci_shared/pickle_state_completeness.py:1-35 (rule description: any class with no __getstate__/__reduce__ that assigns a lock/thread/pool/file/socket/connection outside __init__). No 'is this class ever pickled' test and no suppression marker in the module docstring.
failure_scenario: A service object that owns a worker thread, a lock created lazily or a DB connection is reported although nothing in the program pickles it. The consumer baselines one entry per such class, and the baseline no longer separates classes that travel through joblib/multiprocessing from classes that never leave the process; 37-F7 already showed this gate over-reports.
proposed_fix: Report only classes that are plausibly pickled: referenced in a `pickle.dump(s)`, `joblib.dump`, `Pool.map`/`ProcessPoolExecutor.submit` argument position in the scanned corpus, subclass of an sklearn BaseEstimator, a dataclass, or named in a user-provided `pickled_classes` list. Add `# pickle-ok: <reason>` on the assignment.

evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p4.py: `(127, 32767)` in two modules, `(0.01, 0.05)`, `(0.025, 0.975)` and `(8000, 8080)` -> 1 [literal-set] finding each; `(255, 65535)`, `(429, 503)`, `(0.25, 0.75)`, `(1024, 2048)` -> 0 (in DEFAULT_IGNORE, src/py_ci_shared/drifted_duplicate_literals.py:73-77). Consumer evidence: mlframe _drifted_duplicate_literals_baseline.json has 24 literal-set groups; its own notes call the (127, 32767) group 'int8/int16 dtype bounds ... fixed by the numeric types' and several 'two unrelated defaults that happen to coincide'.
failure_scenario: Standard constants (type limits, confidence levels) become findings the first time two modules write them, and the only per-site exit is the marker, which a reviewer has to remember for every new pair.

title: hash_key_determinism flags `json.dumps` of a dict literal with a fixed key order and of `dataclasses.asdict(obj)` that is hashed without sort_keys
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/probe2.out lines 'hash:dumps_dict_literal' and 'hash:dumps_asdict': `hashlib.sha256(json.dumps({'a': a, 'b': b}).encode())` -> [unsorted-json-key]; `json.dumps(dataclasses.asdict(o))` -> [unsorted-json-key]. Both orders are fixed by source text (literal keys; dataclass field order), so the digest is stable across runs and processes. Not flagged: list literal, str(...), list comprehension.
failure_scenario: Digest keys built from a literal record are reported as non-deterministic. The fix the gate asks for (sort_keys=True) is harmless but changes every existing digest of an on-disk cache, so a consumer prefers to baseline it.
proposed_fix: Treat a dict display whose keys are all string literals, `dataclasses.asdict`, `vars(self)` of a dataclass and `NamedTuple._asdict()` as ordered. Keep flagging a dict built by comprehension over a set or a dict from a parameter.

title: skip_as_pass treats `echo "SKIPPED <optional step>"` followed by `exit 0` after the real checks ran as a skipped guard
evidence: Ran C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/C--Users-Admin/374112a1-797e-4d89-b4ed-a53928a70eeb/scratchpad/audit41/p7.py: tool/c.sh `echo "SKIPPED stale cache" \nexit 0` -> 1 finding; .github step `echo SKIPPED\n exit 0` -> 1. src/py_ci_shared/skip_as_pass.py module docstring 'Approximation: a block is recognised by its shape, not by a parser'. Not flagged: SKIPPED inside an `if ... fi` followed by an outer `exit 0`, `print('SKIPPED files:', 0)` + `return 0`, `passed=3 SKIPPED=0`.
failure_scenario: A script that reports an optional sub-step as skipped and then finishes its real work is listed as skip-as-pass; the baseline needs a note per script. Low volume (opt-in gate, 1 consumer baseline) so the cost is a note, not a block.
proposed_fix: Require that the SKIPPED line is the last statement before the exit in the same block (no command between) or that the exit is the script's only exit path; otherwise the line is a progress message.

title: Tracker rows 37-F35 and 37-F40 carry stale or contradictory text, and 37-F19 stays 'NOT REPRODUCED' without a closing action
